note: A VERDICT SHEET, NOT A SINGLE ANSWER. One row per (group, surviving-reviewer
count), because `state_manager.generate_group_id` hashes the theme plus the
NORMALIZED SUGGESTION LIST and a group holds one member per model that raised
the theme -- so a group's id is a function of HOW MANY REVIEWERS ANSWERED.
Measured 2026-09-22 on tests/container/runs/20260922T084502Z: the same four
themes grouped to one set of ids on the codex host's five-model rows and to
another on the opencode host's four, and to a third (the ids this file used to
ship alone) on every single-spec row. `merge_batched_validation_results`
joins BY HASH and discards a foreign one, and
`subagent_executor._validation_result_errors` requires a group_hash/group_id on
every entry, so a sheet that names one count joins nothing on a row of any
other -- every group lands on validation_failed and the apply phases have
nothing to apply. A sheet naming them all joins the row that belongs to this
batch and lets the merge discard the rest, which is the same mechanism that
already discards this file's OTHER GROUPS on every batch (a batch holds a
subset of the groups); it is one file rather than one per panel because a
per-panel file re-breaks on the next roster move.
WHAT THE ID DEPENDS ON, MEASURED, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. Only the member COUNT
and the suggestion CONTENT. Not which CLIs are in the panel, not their order,
not the host: a five-member opencode panel would reuse the five-member ids
below verbatim. So a carve-out, a roster swap or a reviewer that dies mid-run
(measured: grok on the 2026-09-22 opencode row, leaving four of five) only
picks a different row from this sheet.
RE-CAPTURE THIS FILE WHEN, AND ONLY WHEN:
1. the phase's fan-out fixture changes its suggestions' `type`, `reference`
or `desc` (the first 200 chars), or the number/titles of its entries --
those are the hash's other inputs, and a re-worded fixture moves EVERY
id here;
2. a host's `fan_out:` in tests/container/host_matrix.yaml grows past
6 members, the largest this sheet covers (a SMALLER panel needs
nothing -- every count from 1 up is already here);
3. `state_manager.generate_group_id` changes what it hashes.
A panel that merely changes MEMBERSHIP needs nothing. Re-capture by driving
`suggestion_processor.group_similar_suggestions` + `state_manager.
stamp_stable_ids` over N copies of the fan-out fixture and reading
`generate_group_id` off each group, which is exactly what
`validation_batcher` writes into a batch's `group_ids`.
THIS SHEET IS NOT A PANEL-SIZE ALARM, deliberately. A reviewer that silently
stops answering is caught by `harness.fan_out_correlation` and the matrix's
`fan_out_carve_outs:` cells, which own that question; making the verdicts fail
to join three phases later would only report it as the wrong defect.
